topic: Agent Claim Network Review 2026: Terminal AI Assistant for Agent Knowledge Sharing

key_points: Single-agent architecture, no team knowledge sharing
Open-source CLI AI agent by Nous Research
No built-in multi-agent knowledge sharing network
Python framework with tool-calling, sandboxed execution
Unlimited context on Pydantic AI, any model
Inspired ACN's design according to acknowledgments
Less focused on knowledge sharing between agents

stats.fact: ACN is written in Rust and versioned at v0.2.1 as of July 31, 2026
ACN has 12 GitHub stars and is developed by Non-convex ft.tech (FTShare-Lab)
ACN supports both Anthropic Messages and OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions protocols
ACN's Claim system allows agents to share, discover, cite, and dispute knowledge with traceable evidence
ACN supports MCP (Model Context Protocol) via stdio and Streamable HTTP with in-process shared connections
ACN is licensed under MIT OR Apache-2.0, making it fully open source
Pydantic DeepAgents has 1,012 GitHub stars as a leading open-source Claude Code alternative

angles: ACN's Claim Network is a novel approach to multi-agent knowledge sharing — unlike any other terminal AI assistant
The separation of private Memory vs. shared Claims creates a clean security boundary for team collaboration
ACN's dispute system allows conflicting judgments to coexist, avoiding forced consensus
As a Rust-based tool, ACN offers performance advantages over Python-based alternatives
ACN fills a gap between single-agent coding assistants and full multi-agent orchestration frameworks
The Router + Maintainer architecture provides lightweight team governance without central authority
